findings.reason: a node reading "Why" first is told to build the reportless branch that the section itself says production never raises, which is exactly the defect the section was re-planned to remove.
findings.text: the "Why" paragraph asserts "A staging failure raised before the commit carries no such report, so the function returns False and the receipt takes the already-written branch without ever reading the row", but the section's own "Revised after the first build" and the incident landing record it cites refute this: `~/.config/reckon/crew/runs/r-20261019T080250830060-the-foreign-overrun-pane-is-chosen-by-the-seat/landing.json` records the 10:38:20Z refusal at step `stage` carrying `rollback: {plan file: false, per-run ledger file: true}` — a report present, with the ledger file reverted. So the reportless path was never the incident's path.

findings.reason: the node is dispatched "exact — implement as written", and as written it is told both to build the rejected branch and to selectively keep or drop a branch it cannot find.
findings.text: the superseded "Deliverable" and "Done when" are retained unmarked above the revised pair, so §14 states two contradictory deliverables (reportless read-back; diagnose why `_ledger_holds_row` answered present + restore a tracked write without the index) and two negative controls ("restores the report-only decision"; "restores the read-back that answered present"); it also instructs "Keep, change or drop the first build's reportless branch", presupposing a branch on main that does not exist — the first build `r-20261019T123112426653` was not promoted (`01d20fd3d promote(...): not-run`), head `7a788fd3a` is not an ancestor of `48142d5c`, and `_ledger_row_was_rolled_back` at `reckon/crew/promotion_scope.py:1986` carries only the report branch.

findings.reason: the diagnosis is the deliverable the revision exists for and the only thing that decides which fix is correct; unmeasured, it can be skipped and the gate still passes.
findings.text: the "Revised done when" measures the wording, the restoration and the re-promotion, but carries no measure of the revised deliverable's first half ("First establish, with evidence logged under the run directory, why `_ledger_holds_row` answered present … a memoised read, the aggregate ledger, or another source"); "every log ends in `EXIT=`" is a format rule, not a measure of the diagnosis, so a node can satisfy the gate without producing the diagnosis the section was re-planned around ("Then make it read the row the way a later reader will find it" depends on that answer).

findings.reason: two deliverables on one node means neither has its own closing verdict, so the section cannot be closed on one review.
findings.text: "Revised deliverable" states two independent deliverables — "First establish … why `_ledger_holds_row` answered present" and "Second, make a tracked landing write restorable while the index lock is held" — with independent verdicts (one is a diagnosis whose target file may fall outside the grant, the other a restore-behaviour change in `promotion_scope.py`).

findings.reason: the run id is given in the same sentence, so the reader reaches the file without the section pointer; the pointer is misleading but not load-bearing.
